Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. 2. CHARACTER

Face — her own: a boyish, mischievous tomboy energy; light warm-beige skin with a golden undertone; heart-shaped face; large eyes — deep-set eyes, outer eye corners slightly lifted; thick straight brows; broad soft nose; a wide mouth with softly upturned corners; hazel eyes; a dusting of freckles across nose and cheeks.

Her element, carried in her design: boron: a small, light metalloid with a stubborn, hard heart; borax, the white crystal goldsmiths used as a flux and caravans once carried from Tibetan salt lakes along the Silk Road, later hauled out of Death Valley by twenty-mule teams in the 1880s; burns and colours flames a vivid green; with carbon it forms boron carbide, one of the hardest materials known, armour that stops bullets; in borosilicate glass it lets laboratory flasks survive the flame; its atoms swallow neutrons in reactor control rods; rugged, plain-spoken, dependable.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — MECHA
Costume: she is a female mecha personification — plates, joints, binders and glow lines carry the traits above; the plates must read as solid armor with visible joints, not as cloth or a gown; a back unit may carry the motif. Heavy assault armor of dark matte boron-carbide plates edged in borax white, big thick shoulder and leg armor and large back thrusters glowing vivid green, short rod-shaped control units racked along the thighs, the torso fitted and the waist narrow; small, stubborn, unbreakable; the plates must read as solid armor, not a gown.
Silhouette: heavy assault bulk — big, thick shoulder and leg armor, a broad upper silhouette and large thrusters on the back and legs, while the torso stays fitted and the waist narrow. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette.
Colours: borax crystal white, vivid boron-flame green, dark brown-black amorphous boron, sun-baked desert ochre.
Exposure (bold): her mecha frame is cut open by design in only these places — bare shoulders and upper arms between pauldron and gauntlet, and a deep open chest window with natural cleavage framed by the chest plates; everywhere else she stays fully plated. The plates stay on, fitted and symmetrical, with skin clearly showing in each opening. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; keep the plate material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: year 2200, a desert reactor citadel armoured in dark boron-carbide plate: reactor halls where boron control rods slide down to calm the neutrons, green signal lights along the walls, borosilicate glass domes sheltering farms on the ochre sand.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (B) and atomic number (5) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
